meta.title: Final historical ranking for montage
meta.wealth_note: wealth is now a simplified on-screen value without date or peak-year qualifiers.
meta.country_note: Country reflects the primary public country association used for the final montage dataset.
meta.wealth_source_note: wealth_source is a short plain-English business label for broad audiences.
meta.source_detail_note: source_detail is now written in more natural spoken English, with less corporate phrasing and less repetition.
meta.wealth_origin_note: wealth_origin shows whether the fortune was self-made, inherited, inherited and expanded, widow inheritance, family business, family wealth or divorce settlement.
meta.money_from_note: Use money_from for on-screen cards: it names the business in simple global English first, then the brand in brackets when helpful.
meta.name_note: name is now simplified for display and does not include trailing family markers.

entries.name: Hetty Green
entries.source_detail: She made her money the old Wall Street way, snapping up distressed bonds, making loans and buying property.
entries.fact: Known as the 'Witch of Wall Street,' she was famously frugal but brilliantly ruthless. She snapped up distressed bonds and foreclosed properties to become the wealthiest woman of the Gilded Age.
entries.money_from:
19th Century Financier
Wall Street & Real estate

entries.name: Madam C. J. Walker
entries.source_detail: Her fortune grew out of haircare and beauty products created for Black women.
entries.fact: She was America's first female self-made millionaire. She started with nothing and built an empire selling haircare products specifically designed for Black women.
entries.money_from:
Haircare Pioneer
Beauty products for Black women

entries.name: Annie Turnbo Malone
entries.source_detail: Before Walker, Malone was already making serious money from Poro hair products and beauty training.
entries.fact: Even before Madam C.J. Walker got famous, Malone was quietly building a massive Black-owned beauty business. She made her millions through cosmetics and a nationwide network of beauty schools.

entries.name: Marjorie Merriweather Post
entries.source_detail: The family cereal money was the starting point; she then helped turn it into the much larger General Foods empire.
entries.fact: She turned her family's cereal business into the General Foods empire. She was the original owner of the Mar-a-Lago estate long before it became famous for other reasons.
entries.money_from:
Food Empire Heiress
Post Cereal & General Foods

entries.name: Brooke Astor
entries.source_detail: This was old Astor money, rooted in prime New York real estate.
entries.fact: She married into the legendary Astor dynasty and their vast Manhattan real estate wealth. For decades, her name meant ultimate high society, old money, and huge philanthropic gifts.
entries.money_from:
New York Socialite
Astor real estate fortune

entries.name: Huguette Clark
entries.source_detail: Her wealth was inherited from her father, who made a fortune in copper.
entries.fact: She inherited a massive copper mining fortune but spent decades living entirely out of public sight in hospital rooms. Meanwhile, she owned empty mansions and world-class paintings.

entries.name: Barbara Hutton
entries.source_detail: She was born into the Woolworth store fortune.
entries.fact: The press called her the 'Poor Little Rich Girl.' She inherited the massive Woolworth department store fortune but became famous for her lavish spending and seven turbulent marriages.

entries.name: Doris Duke
entries.source_detail: The Duke billions came from tobacco, electricity and a long list of investments.
entries.fact: She took the billions her family made from tobacco and power companies and spent them on art, world travel, and sprawling estates. She was essentially American royalty.

entries.name: Dirce Navarro De Camargo
entries.source_detail: Her family's wealth was built in Brazil through construction, cement and energy.
entries.fact: She was the quiet force behind a massive Brazilian conglomerate spanning cement, construction, and electricity. She basically built much of Latin America's modern infrastructure.

entries.name: Doris Fisher
entries.source_detail: Gap was the source of her fortune; she built it from one clothing store into a huge chain.
entries.fact: She co-founded Gap to fix a simple problem: her husband couldn't find jeans that fit. From that one store, they built a global fashion empire that defined 90s casual style.

entries.name: Helen Walton
entries.source_detail: Her money came from Walmart, the low-price retail giant built by the Walton family.
entries.fact: She was there when her husband Sam opened the first Walmart. As the business grew into a global heavyweight, she quietly became one of the planet's wealthiest people.

entries.name: Anne Cox Chambers
entries.source_detail: She inherited Cox wealth from newspapers, TV stations and cable systems.
entries.fact: She and her sister inherited a giant newspaper and TV network, then watched its value explode during the cable television boom. She spent 33 years running the massive Cox media empire.

entries.name: Leona Helmsley
entries.source_detail: Hotels and Manhattan real estate made her rich.
entries.fact: Nicknamed the 'Queen of Mean,' she ran a Manhattan hotel empire with an iron fist. She famously went to prison for tax evasion after reportedly claiming 'only the little people pay taxes.'

entries.name: Barbara Cox Anthony
entries.source_detail: She inherited Cox wealth from newspapers, TV stations and cable systems.
entries.fact: She co-owned the mammoth privately-held Cox media empire with her sister. They quietly controlled major newspapers, local TV stations, and a huge chunk of America's cable networks.

entries.name: Liliane Bettencourt
entries.source_detail: Most of her money came from L'Oreal, the beauty empire behind makeup, skincare and hair products.
entries.fact: She was the only child of L'Oréal's founder and became the richest woman in the world. Her final years were overshadowed by a massive scandal involving gifts to a celebrity photographer.

entries.name: Marguerite Harbert
entries.source_detail: The Harbert fortune started in construction and later spread into investments.
entries.fact: She inherited a fortune born in Alabama construction that eventually expanded into global investments. She quietly became one of the wealthiest people in the American South.

entries.name: Birgit Rausing
entries.source_detail: Think drink cartons: the family fortune came from Tetra Pak packaging.
entries.fact: Her fortune comes from a simple invention: the cardboard drink carton. The Tetra Pak changed how the world buys milk and juice, turning her family into billionaires.

entries.name: Johanna Quandt
entries.source_detail: Her fortune was tied to the family's big stake in BMW.
entries.fact: She started as a secretary at BMW, married the boss who saved the company from bankruptcy, and eventually inherited a massive stake. She was one of the prime forces behind the luxury car maker.

entries.name: Joan Kroc
entries.source_detail: She inherited McDonald's money after Ray Kroc died.
entries.fact: She inherited the McDonald's fortune from her husband, Ray Kroc. Instead of hoarding the billions, she became famously generous, secretly giving away vast sums to charity.

entries.name: Kwong Siu-hing
entries.source_detail: Her wealth came from Hong Kong property, especially the giant developer Sun Hung Kai.
entries.fact: She took control of Hong Kong's largest property developer after her husband passed away. She became a central figure in one of Asia's most dramatic wealthy family feuds.
entries.money_from:
Real Estate Matriarch
Sun Hung Kai Properties

entries.name: Susan Thompson Buffett
entries.source_detail: The fortune was tied to Berkshire Hathaway, Warren Buffett's investing empire.
entries.fact: She married Warren Buffett long before he became a billionaire legend. They lived separately for decades but she remained one of the largest shareholders of his massive investment empire.

entries.name: Lily Safra
entries.source_detail: This was banking money, from the Safra family's private-bank fortune.
entries.fact: She married into the intensely secretive Safra banking dynasty. After her husband died in a mysterious fire in Monaco, she became known for her stunning art collection and historic Riviera villas.

entries.name: Eva Gonda de Rivera
entries.source_detail: The family got rich from convenience stores and soft drinks through FEMSA, OXXO and Coca-Cola bottling.
entries.fact: Her family built a Latin American empire based on convenience stores and soft drinks. Thanks to a massive Coca-Cola bottling operation and the ubiquitous OXXO shops, she became Mexico's wealthiest woman.

entries.name: Nina Wang
entries.source_detail: Her fortune came through Chinachem, a Hong Kong business built around property and chemicals.
entries.fact: She famously wore pigtails and lived frugally despite being Asia's richest woman. Her life sounded like a movie: her husband was kidnapped and vanished, leaving her to run a massive property empire.

entries.name: Barbara Piasecka Johnson
entries.source_detail: She became enormously rich through the Johnson & Johnson family fortune.
entries.fact: She arrived in the US from Poland with $100 and got a job as a cook for the Johnson & Johnson heir. She married him, inherited his wealth, and became one of the world's most talked-about billionaires.

entries.name: Judy Love
entries.source_detail: Her money came from Love's, the highway chain of gas stations, truck stops and roadside stores.
entries.fact: She and her husband started with a $5,000 loan and one gas station. They turned it into the massive Love's truck stop empire, proving you don't need tech to make billions in America.
entries.money_from:
Highway Retail Hero
Love's Travel Stops

entries.name: Maria Franca Fissolo
entries.source_detail: This is Ferrero money, from Nutella and other global sweets brands.
entries.fact: She was a secretary who married Michele Ferrero, the man who brought Nutella, Tic Tacs, and Ferrero Rocher to the world. She inherited the keys to Europe's sweetest fortune.

entries.name: Jacqueline Mars
entries.source_detail: She inherited Mars money, from candy, snacks and pet food.
entries.fact: She owns a massive slice of the fiercely private company that makes Snickers, M&Ms, and Pedigree pet food. It's a sweet but quiet inherited fortune that rarely makes headlines.

entries.name: Marilyn Carlson Nelson
entries.source_detail: The fortune came from hotels and travel services through the Carlson group.
entries.fact: She inherited an empire sprawling across hotels and global travel services. Unlike many quiet heirs, she took an active role, broke glass ceilings, and pushed the company forward.

entries.name: Elaine Wynn
entries.source_detail: Las Vegas casinos and luxury hotels were the source of her wealth.
entries.fact: She's the 'Queen of Las Vegas.' She co-founded sprawling casino resorts that defined the modern Strip, then fought highly public board battles to retain her billionaire status after a divorce.

entries.name: Barbara Carlson Gage
entries.source_detail: The fortune came from hotels and travel services through the Carlson group.
entries.fact: Along with her sister, she inherited a global travel and hospitality powerhouse. It's a classic Midwestern American fortune that quietly expanded around the globe.

entries.name: Friede Springer
entries.source_detail: Her money came from Axel Springer, a giant media company built on newspapers, magazines and digital news.
entries.fact: She was a nanny who married the founder of Germany's biggest publishing house. After he died, she took control and transformed the company into a modern digital media giant.

entries.name: Iris Fontbona
entries.source_detail: Mining is at the heart of this fortune, especially copper.
entries.fact: She inherited a massive Chilean copper mining and brewing empire. While staying mostly out of the spotlight, she controls one of the most powerful business groups in Latin America.

entries.name: Massimiliana Landini Aleotti
entries.source_detail: Her wealth comes from Menarini, a major medicines business.
entries.fact: She inherited Menarini, Italy's leading pharmaceutical company. It's an enormous drug empire built quietly over decades, making her one of the very richest women in Europe.

entries.name: Antonia Ax:son Johnson
entries.source_detail: This family fortune was built in trade, energy and industry.
entries.fact: She took over a massive Swedish trading and retail empire from her father. She expanded the old-school industrial business into everything from food to energy across Europe.

entries.name: Charlotte Colket Weber
entries.source_detail: She inherited Campbell Soup money.
entries.fact: Her fortune comes mostly from condensed soup. As a major heir to the Campbell Soup empire, she used her wealth to become a massive patron of art and thoroughbred horse racing.

entries.name: Rosalia Mera
entries.source_detail: She co-built the business that became Zara and the Inditex fashion empire.
entries.fact: She dropped out of school to become a seamstress. Along with her ex-husband, she started making clothes at home—and built Zara into a business that completely changed global fashion.

entries.name: Elaine Marshall
entries.source_detail: Her fortune comes from Koch Industries, a private giant in oil, chemicals, fertilizer and pipelines.
entries.fact: She married into a major stake of the intensely private Koch Industries. It's an empire built on oil, chemicals, and pipelines, making her a silent billionaire powerhouse.

entries.name: Miriam Adelson
entries.source_detail: Casino resorts made this fortune.
entries.fact: She was a doctor researching drug addiction before she married billionaire Sheldon Adelson. Now she controls a massive empire of mega-casinos spanning from Vegas to Macau.

entries.name: Rafaela Aponte-Diamant
entries.source_detail: She built her wealth in cargo shipping, moving containers around the world by sea.
entries.fact: She and her husband started with a single cargo ship and built MSC into the world's biggest container line. It's an incredibly rare case of a massive self-made logistics fortune.

entries.name: Diane Hendricks
entries.source_detail: She made her fortune selling roofing, siding and other construction supplies.
entries.fact: She co-founded a roofing and siding distributor and turned it into an absolute juggernaut. Today she's America's wealthiest self-made woman, purely through selling construction materials.

entries.name: Sherry Brydson
entries.source_detail: This is old media money, tied to Thomson Reuters and related holdings.
entries.fact: Her fortune comes from a massive Canadian media and financial data empire. She keeps an incredibly low profile while holding a giant stake in the Thomson Reuters holding company.

entries.name: Ann Walton Kroenke
entries.source_detail: She inherited part of the Walmart fortune.
entries.fact: As a niece of Walmart founder Sam Walton, she inherited massive stock holdings. She's also married to sports mogul Stan Kroenke, combining retail billions with major league sports.

entries.name: Alice Walton
entries.source_detail: She inherited part of the Walmart fortune.
entries.fact: She is the daughter of Walmart founder Sam Walton. Instead of working at the family company, she used her retail billions to curate one of the world's finest private art collections.

entries.name: Christy Walton
entries.source_detail: Her wealth came from the Walmart fortune after her husband's death.
entries.fact: She married into the Walmart dynasty. After her husband died in a tragic plane crash, she instantly became one of the wealthiest women on earth thanks to his stock holdings.

entries.name: Miuccia Prada
entries.source_detail: She turned Prada into a global luxury-fashion powerhouse.
entries.fact: She took over her grandfather's modest luggage company and transformed it into a global high-fashion powerhouse. She basically defined intellectual luxury clothing for decades.

entries.name: Christina Onassis
entries.source_detail: The money came from the Onassis shipping fortune.
entries.fact: She was the sole surviving heir to Aristotle Onassis' legendary shipping fortune. Her life was a mix of unimaginable jet-set luxury and deep personal tragedy.

entries.name: Mary Alice Dorrance Malone
entries.source_detail: She inherited Campbell Soup money.
entries.fact: She is the largest shareholder of the Campbell Soup Company. Her immense fortune comes from a simple pantry staple, allowing her to live quietly while investing in equestrian estates.

entries.name: Blair Parry-Okeden
entries.source_detail: Her fortune came from Cox, a media and cable empire.
entries.fact: She inherited a quarter of the vast Cox media and automotive empire. Though she grew up in the US, she moved to Australia and quietly became the richest person in the country.

entries.name: Esther Koplowitz
entries.source_detail: She became rich through FCC, a business built on construction, water systems and city services.
entries.fact: She inherited a colossal Spanish construction and public services company. She managed to buy out her sister and navigate massive corporate battles while maintaining her billionaire status.

entries.name: Savitri Jindal
entries.source_detail: The family money came from steel, power and big infrastructure projects.
entries.fact: After her husband died in a helicopter crash, she took over the sprawling Jindal empire spanning steel, mining, and power generation. She is now the wealthiest woman in India.

entries.name: Beate Heister
entries.source_detail: She inherited Aldi supermarket money.
entries.fact: She is the notoriously secretive heir to the Aldi discount supermarket fortune. Millions of people buy cheap groceries there every week, steadily adding to her massive wealth.

entries.name: Carrie Perrodo
entries.source_detail: Her wealth comes from Perenco, an oil and gas business.
entries.fact: Originally a model from Singapore, she inherited the privately-owned oil company Perenco after her husband's death in a climbing accident. The family has kept the business quietly printing money.

entries.name: Marilyn Simons
entries.source_detail: This fortune was made in hedge funds, through Renaissance Technologies.
entries.fact: Her husband founded the world's most successful algorithmic hedge fund. Instead of just hoarding the massive tech-finance wealth, she directs billions into advanced scientific and math research.

entries.name: Nancy Walton Laurie
entries.source_detail: She inherited part of the Walmart fortune.
entries.fact: Inheriting a fortune from the Walmart empire, she and her family use the dividends for massive investments spanning real estate, dance studios, and professional sports teams.

entries.name: Kirsten Rausing
entries.source_detail: Packaging made this fortune, especially the drink-carton business behind Tetra Laval.
entries.fact: She sits on the board of the Tetra Pak packaging giant. Living in the UK, she spends much of her incredible wealth breeding world-class racehorses at her own stud farm.

entries.name: Vicky Safra
entries.source_detail: The money came from the Safra banking empire.
entries.fact: Following her husband's passing, she took over a 180-year-old banking dynasty that stretches across the globe. She is now at the center of one of South America's deepest banking fortunes.

entries.name: Francoise Bettencourt Meyers
entries.source_detail: Most of her wealth comes from L'Oreal.
entries.fact: She is the granddaughter of L'Oréal's founder and the richest woman on the planet. Despite her staggering cosmetics fortune, she is heavily focused on writing books about Greek gods.

entries.name: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
entries.source_detail: She built her fortune in biotech, especially medicines like insulin.
entries.fact: She started a biotech company in her garage in India when nobody believed in female entrepreneurs. Today, she's a self-made billionaire making affordable insulin and life-saving drugs.

entries.name: Alicia Koplowitz
entries.source_detail: She started with construction money and turned a lot of it into investments.
entries.fact: She sold her share in the family construction business to her sister and turned the cash into an incredibly successful private investment fund, proving her own financial genius.

entries.name: Charlene de Carvalho-Heineken
entries.source_detail: Her wealth comes from Heineken beer.
entries.fact: She is the controlling shareholder of Heineken, inheriting the massive stake from her father. In one smooth transition, she took control of one of the world's most famous beer brands.

entries.name: Gina Rinehart
entries.source_detail: Mining made her rich, especially iron ore.
entries.fact: She took her father's struggling iron ore company and aggressively turned it into a colossal mining empire. She is the undisputed, tough-talking queen of the Australian outback.

entries.name: Oprah Winfrey
entries.source_detail: Her money came from television, production deals and owning media businesses.
entries.fact: She escaped profound poverty to build a television talk show that completely changed modern culture. She owns her show, her network, and her brand, making her the ultimate self-made media billionaire.

entries.name: Ronda Stryker
entries.source_detail: She inherited the fortune behind Stryker's hospital beds, surgical tools and medical equipment.
entries.fact: Her grandfather invented a mobile hospital bed and started a medical equipment company. That business exploded into a global healthcare giant, securing her billions in stock.

entries.name: Trudy Cathy White
entries.source_detail: The family money comes from Chick-fil-A restaurants.
entries.fact: She inherited the wildly popular Chick-fil-A franchise. It's a unique fast-food fortune because the family has kept it completely private and still famously closes all locations on Sundays.

entries.name: Shari Arison
entries.source_detail: Her wealth traces back to cruise ships and banking.
entries.fact: She inherited a massive fortune drawn from Israeli banking and the Carnival cruise line. She then transitioned into high-profile global philanthropy and impact investing.
entries.money_from:
Banking & Cruise Heiress
Carnival Cruises & Banking

entries.name: Zhang Yin
entries.source_detail: She made her money turning recycled paper into cardboard and packaging.
entries.fact: She saw value where others saw trash. She made billions by importing scrap paper from the US to China and recycling it into ubiquitous cardboard shipping boxes.

entries.name: Valerie Mars
entries.source_detail: She inherited Mars money, from candy, snacks and pet food.
entries.fact: She is part of the massively wealthy, intensely private Mars family. Every time you buy an M&M, Snickers, or even Whiskas cat food, you're adding to her fortune.

entries.name: Abigail Johnson
entries.source_detail: Her fortune comes from Fidelity, which manages savings, retirement money and investment funds.
entries.fact: She didn't just inherit the massive Fidelity mutual fund empire; she runs it. She was also one of the first major Wall Street CEOs to aggressively embrace cryptocurrency.

entries.name: Zhong Huijuan
entries.source_detail: She built her wealth in prescription medicines.
entries.fact: She quit her job as a chemistry teacher to start a pharmaceutical company. She turned it into a massive drug manufacturer, becoming one of the most successful self-made women in Asia.

entries.name: Margarita Louis-Dreyfus
entries.source_detail: This is commodity-trading money: grain, cotton and other raw materials.
entries.fact: Look at the grain or cotton in your house—her company probably shipped it. After inheriting a centuries-old trading empire from her husband, she successfully consolidated her control over it.

entries.name: Susanne Klatten
entries.source_detail: Her wealth comes from BMW on one side and chemicals on the other.
entries.fact: She holds sweeping stakes in BMW and an international chemical company. To protect her privacy, she once worked under an assumed name in her own company to learn the business.

entries.name: Laurene Powell Jobs
entries.source_detail: A lot of her money comes from Apple and Disney shares, plus investments of her own.
entries.fact: After Steve Jobs passed away, she inherited massive stakes in Apple and Disney. Rather than sitting back, she launched an aggressively active investing and social impact firm.

entries.name: Maria Asuncion Aramburuzabala
entries.source_detail: The fortune started with Corona beer money and grew further through investments.
entries.fact: Her family gave the world Corona beer. After selling the brewery, she took her immense wealth, became a ruthless venture capitalist, and established herself as a titan in Mexican business.
entries.money_from:
Brewery & Real Estate Heiress
Corona (Grupo Modelo)

entries.name: Yelena Baturina
entries.source_detail: She made her money in real estate and construction materials.
entries.fact: As the wife of Moscow's former mayor, she built a staggering fortune in Russian real estate and construction. For a long time, she was the only female billionaire in Russia.

entries.name: Melinda French Gates
entries.source_detail: Most of her wealth came from Microsoft-related assets and later investments.
entries.fact: She helped build the world's most powerful philanthropic foundation. Following her towering divorce from Bill Gates, she emerged with her own immense tech fortune and a new investing identity.

entries.name: Wu Yajun
entries.source_detail: She got rich building homes and residential property in China.
entries.fact: She started as a factory worker and journalist before building one of China's premier housing developers from scratch. She is the definition of a relentlessly driven self-made titan.

entries.name: J. K. Rowling
entries.source_detail: Harry Potter is where the money came from: books, films, royalties and related products.
entries.fact: She wrote a story about a wizard on a delayed train while living on state benefits. It became the best-selling book series in history, spinning off films, theme parks, and billions.

entries.name: Marijke Mars
entries.source_detail: She inherited Mars money, from candy, snacks and pet food.
entries.fact: Like her sisters, she inherited a chunk of the privately-held Mars candy and pet empire. It remains one of the quietest and most stable billionaire fortunes in American business.

entries.name: Denise Coates
entries.source_detail: She built her fortune in online betting and casino games.
entries.fact: She bought the domain Bet365 on eBay and launched a sports betting site from a portable cabin. Today, she routinely ranks as one of the highest-paid chief executives in the entire world.

entries.name: Renata Kellnerova
entries.source_detail: The family money came from lending, telecom and investments through PPF.
entries.fact: Her husband died in a tragic Alaskan helicopter crash, leaving her control of a massive Czech conglomerate. The empire touches everything from consumer lending to telecommunications across Eastern Europe.

entries.name: Wang Laichun
entries.source_detail: She made her money supplying cables, connectors and other parts for phones and electronics.
entries.fact: She spent 10 years working on Foxconn assembly lines before quitting to start her own electronics company. Now she makes billions supplying critical parts for Apple's AirPods and iPhones.

entries.name: Sandra Ortega Mera
entries.source_detail: She inherited a big stake in Zara's parent company.
entries.fact: She is the daughter of the founders of the Zara fashion empire. Unlike many billionaires, she keeps a fiercely private life, shunning the press and focusing completely on philanthropy.

entries.name: MacKenzie Scott
entries.source_detail: Most of her money came from Amazon shares she received after her divorce from Jeff Bezos.
entries.fact: She was married to Jeff Bezos for 25 years before their divorce gave her a massive stake in Amazon. She instantly became wealthier than most monarchs—and immediately started giving it all away.

entries.name: Zhou Qunfei
entries.source_detail: She got rich making smartphone screens and touch glass.
entries.fact: She dropped out of school to make watch lenses. Eventually, she pioneered the massive glass screens used on smartphones, supplying giants like Apple and Samsung to make her billions.

entries.name: Sara Blakely
entries.source_detail: She built her fortune selling Spanx shapewear.
entries.fact: She cut the feet off her pantyhose to make smoothing undergarments, patenting the idea herself. Spanx became an absolute phenomenon, placing her entirely organically into the billionaire club.

entries.name: Lyndal Stephens Greth
entries.source_detail: This is oil money, built in the energy business.
entries.fact: Her billionaire status materialized almost overnight after her family's intensely private Texas oil business exploded in value, showcasing how raw natural resources still mint ultra-wealth.

entries.name: Tatyana Kim
entries.source_detail: She made her money by turning Wildberries into a giant online store for clothes, shoes and everyday goods.
entries.fact: While on maternity leave, she started reselling clothes she ordered from German catalogs. It exploded into Wildberries, turning her into Russia's undisputed e-commerce queen.

entries.name: Julia Koch
entries.source_detail: Her fortune comes from Koch Industries, which makes money from oil, chemicals, fertilizer, pipelines and trading.
entries.fact: When her husband David Koch passed away, she inherited a massive chunk of his fiercely private industrial empire. She essentially went from socialite to one of the richest people on Earth.

entries.name: Yang Huiyan
entries.source_detail: She became rich through one of China's biggest homebuilding companies.
entries.fact: Before she even turned 30, her father transferred massive shares in his gigantic Chinese property development firm to her name, briefly making her the outright richest woman in Asia.

entries.name: Athina Onassis
entries.source_detail: What remained of the family wealth came from the Onassis shipping fortune.
entries.fact: She is the sole surviving heir to legendary shipping magnate Aristotle Onassis. Despite growing up with staggering wealth and media attention, her actual liquid fortune turned out smaller than legends claimed.

entries.name: Rihanna
entries.source_detail: Most of her money came from beauty and lingerie businesses, not from music.
entries.fact: Everyone knows her as a singer, but music didn't make her a billionaire. She created a makeup line for all skin tones and completely disrupted the global beauty industry.
entries.money_from:
Singer & Business Tycoon
Fenty Beauty & Savage X

entries.name: Taylor Swift
entries.source_detail: Her fortune was built on songs, streaming and enormous concert tours.
entries.fact: Forget selling makeup or running hedge funds. She achieved billionaire status almost entirely through the sheer, unprecedented success of her songwriting, streaming rights, and colossal global tours.
entries.money_from:
Singer & Songwriter
Music catalogue & Eras Tour
